items.item_text: Possession of a master’s degree or higher from an accredited college or university. (See our website for evaluation requirements for units and degrees earned at foreign institutions). All required degrees must be earned and conferred by the position start date of January 1, 2027; and
Possession of a Ph.D., Ed.D., or terminal degree;
Knowledge of teaching and learning strategies and experience in evaluation of those strategies;
Five years of increasingly responsible full-time administrative experience in an institution of higher education.
At least three years of teaching experience at the college or university level; community college teaching experience is preferred;
A track record of being innovative in planning, developing and producing quality instruction and student services delivered via technology;
Familiar with provisions of the California Education Code, the California Code of Regulations, and federal regulations that bear on the operations of the college.
Build community partnerships and engagement, which aims to build deep connections with community organizations and employers to promote education, career advancement, and transfer opportunities;
Proficiency in applying technological applications to daily responsibilities;
Commitment to access, success, and equity for all populations;
A heightened sense of integrity, high energy, devotion to collegiality and civility as the accepted mode of discourse, and an exceptional level of creativity and initiative;
Knowledge of the mission of California Community Colleges; education code, Title 5 regulations, and accreditation standards;
Understanding of the curriculum process and ability to develop and implement credit and not-for-credit programs;
Ability to relate well and work effectively with students, faculty, staff and business and industry representatives of diverse backgrounds to achieve the college’s strategic priority.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a participatory manner with all segments of the college community and community at large;
Ability to lead, implement, and manage change;
Ability to interpret and uniformly implement district policies and procedures and the District bargaining agreements;

A commitment and sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socioeconomic, ethnic, cultural, disability, religious background and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff as well as commitment to integrating diversity in the College’s instructional program;
Ability to manage and direct staff with diverse responsibilities and simultaneous projects in a team environment and achieve conflict resolution; and
Ability to communicate effectively and persuasively orally, in writing, and using technology.
